To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Gauss-Bonnett correction to gravity may lead to a revival of the quartic inflation model and the standard consistency relation for the tensor-to-spectral index of tensor perturbation is broken.

the Gauss-Bon-net correction to the Einstein-Hilbert action may significantly change predictions of inflation models and that the Gauss-Bonneterm with a positive (negative) coupling may lead, respectively, to a reduction (enhancement) of the tensor-scalar ratio and may revive the quartice potential ruled out by the recent cosmological data.
the Gauss-BonNet term with a positive coupling may reduce the tensor-to-scar ratio, and hence may revive a quartic potential ruled-out by recent cosmological observations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the slow-roll inflation with a scalar field nonminimally coupled to the Gauss-Bonneterm.
the slow-roll inflation with a nonminimal coupling between a scalar field and the Gauss-BonNet term, which may be relevant to a higher-dimensional gravity theory.
the effects of a nonminimal coupling to a Gauss-Bon-net term in the action of a scalar field on the cosmological evolution of the Universe and the production of primordial perturbations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Gauss-Bonnett correction may lead to a significant reduction of the tensor-to scalar ratio, but the tensor-to scalar power ratio is still too small to be detectable by the next generation of CMB experiments.
the Gauss-Bon-net term can be safely neglected in the slow-roll regime.
the Gauss-Bonnett corrections may lead to a more complicated and rich cosmological phenomenology than the usual inflation models.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Gauss-Bonner term can be a promising alternative to the standard slow-roll inflation with a canonical scalar field.
, in general, the Gauss-BonNet term can not be ignored during inflation.
the Gauss-Bonnett term with a negative coupling can be used to enhance the tensor perturbations and hence may be used to revive the quartic and other models of inflation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, even if the tensor-to-sclar ratio is close to the upper bound set by the 7 year Wilkinson Microwave Anisotropic Probe data, the Gauss-Bon-net term may still play a significant role in inflation.
the presence of the Gauss-Bon-net correction may lead to a significant change in the inflationary predictions and hence may have important implications for the inflationary model building.
, for a given potential, the Gauss-BonNet correction may significantly affect the inflationary dynamics and hence the power spectra of perturbations.
